subsystems.name: Liquid metal cell
subsystems.role: the core electrochemistry: three molten layers that separate themselves by density and immiscibility, so there is no solid membrane to wear out.
parts: light-metal anode (calcium, magnesium, sodium or lithium) floating on top
molten salt electrolyte in the middle
dense heavy-metal alloy cathode (antimony, bismuth or lead) at the bottom

subsystems.name: Hermetic enclosure and seals
subsystems.role: keeps oxygen and moisture away from highly reactive molten metals at several hundred degrees.
parts: corrosion-resistant current collectors (often tungsten or molybdenum)

subsystems.name: Thermal system
subsystems.role: holds every cell above its melting point, and handles the heat generated during charging and discharging.

subsystems.name: Module and container
subsystems.role: groups cells into a transportable, serviceable unit.

subsystems.name: Power conversion and controls
subsystems.role: converts DC to grid AC and manages state of charge, temperature and grid signals.

buildSteps.title: Choose and purify the chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Specific grades of the light anode metal, the heavy cathode metal and the halide salt are selected; trace impurities can raise melting points or corrode the cell.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the cell layers
buildSteps.detail: Measured amounts of the metals and salt are placed into the can in the correct order, so that once molten they settle into anode, electrolyte and cathode.

buildSteps.title: Seal the cell
buildSteps.detail: Ceramic-metal seals and welded lids close the can. This is the hardest step: the seal must survive hundreds of degrees, thermal cycling and attack by molten salt.

buildSteps.title: Insulate and instrument
buildSteps.detail: The sealed cell is wrapped in high-temperature insulation and fitted with heaters and temperature sensors.

buildSteps.title: Rack into modules
buildSteps.detail: Cells are stacked into racks with busbars and thermal control to form a container-scale unit.

buildSteps.title: Commission
buildSteps.detail: Heat-up power melts the layers. The first charge confirms the stack is working and that no cell is leaking or shorted.

buildSteps.title: Operate
buildSteps.detail: During discharge, anode metal gives up electrons and alloys into the cathode; charging reverses this. Heating and pumping parasitics are continuously managed, and the plant must avoid letting cells freeze solid.

buildSteps.title: End of life
buildSteps.detail: Cells are drained and the metals and salt are recovered and re-refined, which suits a chemistry built from commodity metals.

prerequisites.why: calcium, magnesium, antimony and lead are abundant and cheap, but antimony supply is small and concentrated.
long-lived ceramic-metal seals against molten salt remain a reliability challenge.
tungsten and molybdenum resist molten metals and salts, but add cost.
the battery must be kept molten whether or not it is cycling, and that parasitic load cuts round-trip efficiency.
no one has yet built liquid metal cells on automated lines at the volume grid storage needs.

pathway.milestone: cell and container-scale demonstrations of roughly tens to a few hundred kilowatt-hours
pathway.unlocks: the operating data needed to judge calendar life and freeze-thaw survival.

pathway.milestone: multi-megawatt-hour installations with several hours of duration, competing with lithium-ion on cost per cycle rather than efficiency
pathway.unlocks: a durable, non-flammable option for daily cycling on the grid.

pathway.milestone: automated cell production and a secured metals supply chain
pathway.unlocks: falling capital cost and the ability to build many projects at once — the point at which a developer fell short.

pathway.milestone: very long duration storage, days rather than hours, using inexpensive abundant metals
pathway.unlocks: firming high shares of wind and solar without gas turbines.
